theory.intro: The **derivative** $f'(x)$ is the gradient of the tangent to $y=f(x)$ at the point $(x, f(x))$. It gives the instantaneous rate of change of $y$ with respect to $x$.
facts: The derivative of $y=f(x)$ is written $f'(x)$, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ or $y'$, and equals $\lim_{h\to 0}\dfrac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}$ when this limit exists as a finite value.
The gradient of the **secant line** through $(a, f(a))$ and $(b, f(b))$ is the **average rate of change** $\dfrac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$ over $[a, b]$.
The gradient of the **tangent line** at $x=a$ is the **instantaneous rate of change** there, written $f'(a)$.
The derivative exists at $x=a$ when the tangent exists and is not vertical.

workedExamples.question_text: The tangent to $y=f(x)$ at $P(4,3)$ passes through $Q(1,9)$. Find $f'(4)$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The derivative is the gradient of the tangent.
$\begin{align*}f'(4)&=\frac{3-9}{4-1}\\&=\frac{-6}{3}\\&=-2\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text:
The graph shows a curve and its tangent at $P$. Find $f'(3)$ using the labelled points on the tangent.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[x=0.8cm,y=0.65cm,every node/.style={font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont,text=black}]\definecolor{curveBlue}{HTML}{268CFF}\definecolor{tangentOrange}{HTML}{EF8B2C}\draw[black,->] (0,0)--(6,0) node[right] {$x$};\draw[black,->] (0,0)--(0,7) node[above] {$y$};\draw[curveBlue,thick,domain=0.5:5.5,samples=60] plot (\x,{0.4*(\x-3)*(\x-3)+\x-1});\draw[tangentOrange,thick] (1,0)--(6,5);\fill[black] (3,2) circle (2pt);\fill[black] (5,4) circle (2pt);\path (3,2) node[below right] {$P(3,2)$};\path (5,4) node[below right] {$Q(5,4)$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
workedExamples.solution_text:
Read the two labelled points on the orange tangent.
$\begin{align*}f'(3)&=\frac{4-2}{5-3}\\&=\frac{2}{2}\\&=1\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A secant joins two distinct points on a curve. A tangent has the same local gradient as the curve at $x=a$. Which line gives the average rate of change, and which gives $f'(a)$?
workedExamples.solution_text: The secant gradient gives the average rate of change between its two points. The tangent gradient gives the instantaneous rate of change at $x=a$, written $f'(a)$.

workedExamples.question_text: A secant joins $P(d,F(d))$ and $Q(d+r,F(d+r))$, where $r\ne0$. Find its gradient, then explain how it defines $F'(d)$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Rise: $F(d+r)-F(d)$.
Run: $(d+r)-d=r$.
$m_{\text{secant}}=\frac{F(d+r)-F(d)}{r}$.
As $r$ approaches zero, the secant gradient approaches the tangent gradient, provided the limit exists as a finite value.
$F'(d)=\lim_{r\to0}\frac{F(d+r)-F(d)}{r}$.

foundation.question_text:
The tangent line to $y=f(x)$ at $(3, 5)$ passes through $(5, 11)$.
Find the value of $f'(3)$.

The graph shows a curve and its tangent at $P$. Find $f'(2)$ using the labelled points on the tangent.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[x=0.65cm,y=0.4cm]\draw[->] (0,0)--(5,0) node[right] {$x$};\draw[->] (0,0)--(0,10) node[above] {$y$};\draw[blue,thick,domain=0.5:4.5,samples=50] plot (\x,{0.5*(\x-2)^2+2*\x-1});\draw[orange,thick] (0.5,0)--(4.5,8);\fill (2,3) circle (2pt) node[above left] {$P(2,3)$};\fill (4,7) circle (2pt) node[right] {$(4,7)$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
State whether the gradient of the secant line between $x=1$ and $x=5$ on a distance-time graph represents average speed or instantaneous speed.
foundation.solution_text: A secant line between two distinct points represents the average speed over that interval.

foundation.question_text: Name the geometric line whose gradient gives the instantaneous rate of change of a curve at a single point $x=a$.
foundation.solution_text: The tangent line to the curve at $x=a$.
